2026 / North America / Print / exhibit

Average Roll-up Banner

A placeholder baseline for a single retractable event banner with printed graphic, aluminum cassette, and limited reuse.

Project typeEvent display
RatingBaseline
Carbon estimate18 kg CO2e
Waste estimate4 kg
Lifespan5 uses
RecyclabilityMedium

Baseline Scope

This starter baseline describes a common roll-up banner used at events, conferences, and temporary displays.

From studies on PVC banners and aluminum display products, typical findings:

Material production dominates impact (often 50–80%)

PVC is a major environmental burden

Toxic additives (plasticizers, stabilizers)

End-of-life challenges

Aluminum has high upfront impact but good recyclability

Short lifespan = worst-case scenario

Use Notes

Treat all quantitative values as assumptions.

Replace estimates with supplier, transport, and disposal data before using this as evidence.

Keep SD Standard criteria as IDs only in frontmatter.

Design Improvement Opportunities

Service models (renting display systems)

Modular reuse systems (swap graphics, keep base)

Material innovation (PVC-free substrates)

Digital substitution (when appropriate)

Assumptions

Production

  • Assumption only: one standard 33 in x 80 in retractable banner is produced.
  • Assumption only: banner is printed using common wide-format production methods.

Material

  • Assumption only: mixed aluminum, plastic, vinyl or polyester graphic, and carry bag.
  • Assumption only: no verified supplier-specific material declaration is available.

Transport

  • Assumption only: one regional shipment from printer to client or venue.

Disposal

  • Assumption only: graphic may be landfilled if not designed for replacement or recycling.

Placeholder estimate for content modeling and comparison. Not verified LCA data.

Criteria

  • E1 / EnvironmentEnvironmental Impact Reduction

    The project strategy includes at least one action to reduce environmental impact that is supported by a qualified life cycle study (LCS) or quantitative life cycle assessment (LCA).

  • E4 / EnvironmentInk, Printing, and Finishes

    The project reduces or eliminates the use of inks, varnishes and finishes, or requires no printing.

  • E6 / EnvironmentProduct Quantity

    Reproduction is limited to immediate needs, including the possibility that no physical copies were needed.

  • E7 / EnvironmentDurability & Extended Life

    The product or system is physically durable and has a longer life than the industry average, where desirable. The product or system can be reused, recharged, repaired, and/or upgraded as an environmental benefit.

  • F2 / FinanceProfitability

    The project budget or contract financially compensates the design entity.
